answer: Canyon-Knoll Admission Gate. New identities must submit a random-arrival trace over a fixed window; the gate compares inter-arrival gaps against a canyon of expected spacing, rejecting bursts that cluster too tightly. Admitted agents also publish a hollow schedule of future check-ins, so impersonators must precommit to timing they cannot cheaply fake. An attacker pays per identity: sustained waiting, unique scheduling, and idle capacity across the whole window, making mass registration slow and costly.
